q: Too much of childhood is being spent on screens, while sport, hobbies and other after-school activities are out of reach for too many families.
c: Announcing Labour's $7m-a-year Kids Off Screens policy (RNZ).

q: We now have a situation where a government made active decisions to knowingly potentially disenfranchise up to 400,000 New Zealanders from exercising their democratic right to vote.
c: Speaking to reporters about the government's removal of same-day enrolment, as the 25 October enrolment deadline nears (RNZ). The 400,000 figure is her claim.

q: We are not proposing to spend years and millions of dollars studying whether Cantabrians might catch a train. We are proposing to put the trains on and find out.
c: Announcing in Christchurch NZ First's 12-month commuter rail trial for Canterbury (RNZ).

q: There is no time to waste when around 60,000 children start school every year. The work is not finished, but the early signs show why this government has been so relentlessly focused on evidence, implementation and getting support into classrooms quickly.
c: Told RNZ for its analysis of the government's education changes this term (curriculum rewrite, NCEA replacement). Labour would freeze the NCEA reforms.

q: It is a hard slog sometimes, and it's nice to know you're not doing it alone.
c: On ACT's 'Big Pinky' campaign bus on Sunday 18 October, about candidates campaigning together (RNZ feature).

q: We can't necessarily live on milk powder and mutton.
c: Organics Aotearoa New Zealand 'Vote Organic' webinar (5 Oct), on food security after the McCain's and Wattie's factory closures. Reported by the organic-sector news site Organic Food Together, which links the full recording.

q: We're a biological economy.
c: Same webinar, calling cuts to bioeconomy science funding shortsighted (as reported by Organic Food Together).

q: We never quite made that line.
c: Same webinar, on the Gene Technology Bill: the coalition agreement left NZ First open to liberalising gene technology with assurances on human health and the environment (as reported by Organic Food Together).

q: If you guys are voting purely based on organics, I don't believe that we have the best policy platform for you.
c: Closing remark in Organics Aotearoa New Zealand's 'Vote Organic' webinar (5 Oct), as agriculture spokesperson. Reported by the organic-sector news site Organic Food Together, which links the full recording.

q: We think there's a world in which we can do both.
c: Same webinar, asked whether New Zealand can protect its GE-free export status while allowing gene technology. Opportunity opposes the current Gene Technology Bill (as reported by Organic Food Together).

q: I don't know if that's the job of politicians.
c: Same webinar, asked to commit to a higher verification exemption threshold for small organic growers; he said he was six weeks into the agriculture role (as reported by Organic Food Together).

q: When our creativity is strong, our people are strong.
c: Te Pāti Māori press release announcing an independent Toi Māori Authority and an income programme for Māori artists, in Ōtautahi (via Scoop).
s: Te Pāti Māori release via Scoop

q: Christopher Luxon doesn't want to talk about it, but everyone else does. So today, I'm challenging Christopher Luxon: come and debate me on health.
c: In a social media video challenging Luxon to a debate on health, after Luxon denied the health system was in crisis (RNZ).

q: I have no time for the gangs. They will not get any support from any government that I lead.
c: Rejecting Oriini Kaipara's promise to 'restore mana' to Mongrel Mob members; he also said Labour would not support changes to the gang patch ban (RNZ).

q: They are not Probus or the Lions or Rotary, they're not a community organisation, they peddle misery and death and suffering.
c: Responding to Oriini Kaipara's comments on the Mongrel Mob (RNZ).

q: To all the decent centrist Labour supporters, these are the idiots that Chris Hipkins and Labour are going to be in government with.
c: Speaking to reporters in Hamilton about the Green and Te Pāti Māori MPs who attended a Mongrel Mob hui, in a pitch to centrist Labour voters (RNZ live blog).

q: I'm hoping that we can get something put together before Christmas - would be ideal. But frankly, it'll take as long as it takes.
c: RNZ Morning Report weekly interview, asked whether coalition talks would be finished by Christmas. He said formal talks would probably wait for the official count on 27 November (RNZ).

q: I think what we need to clarify first Guyon is the fact you see Mongrel Mob, I see whānau.
c: RNZ Midday Report interview, defending her promise during a gang-pad visit to 'restore mana' to Mongrel Mob members (RNZ).

q: I am not dismissing the stark realities and the violence and the crimes committed by many a gang, not just this one.
c: Same Midday Report interview, accepting the history of violence in gang culture (RNZ).

q: Oriini Kaipara made those comments, not the Green Party, and that is for Te Pāti Māori to answer to.
c: Asked whether the Greens also wanted to 'restore mana' to the Mongrel Mob (RNZ).

q: Labour’s announcement to ban social media for under 16 year olds is a naive solution to a genuine issue.
c: X post responding to Labour's online safety policy.

q: We will ensure it is written into law that every company, bank, organisation, or government office must accept cash for payment and transactions.
c: X post announcing that NZ First has legislation ready to require cash to be accepted.

q: it's essential we don't have a change of government at this time and it's also essential, in my view, that the new coalition has more ACT in it so we can actually grapple with these challenges
c: RNZ First Up interview; he said ACT's job was to ensure the coalition is re-elected (RNZ live blog).

q: Te Pāti Māori say they want to restore their mana. They have none. They lost it when they chose a life where their profits come from the misery of others.
c: ACT press release responding to Oriini Kaipara's comments about restoring mana to Mongrel Mob members.

q: If re-elected, National will get it under construction early next year.
c: National release 'Backing Waikato', on the SH1 Cambridge to Piarere extension of the Waikato Expressway.

q: You've got partners that want to be in coalition with the Mongrel Mob, my friend.
c: Final Stuff leaders' debate, replying after Hipkins criticised Luxon's foreign minister.

q: Yes, that instinctively is a position of the National Party. But I do want to work in a cross-party way with Chris to try and have a proper conversation about retirement.
c: Final Stuff leaders' debate, on raising the superannuation age.

q: We know that what we've been doing is the right stuff. We just want more time, and we need another three years to get the job done.
c: Campaigning on the day the India FTA came into force, asked about the 1News–Verian poll.

q: That was a mistake. Supporting meth addiction is absolutely something governments should do, but giving the money to the gangs is wrong.
c: Morning Report, on the former Labour government funding the Mongrel Mob-run Kahukura programme (RNZ live blog).

q: If you won't listen to the doctors and the nurses who are telling you the health system is in crisis, then you are never going to be able to fix it.
c: Final Stuff leaders' debate, saying Luxon was 'in denial'.

q: It's not right to say that future generations of New Zealanders should pay for the retirement of today's retirees and then not get that themselves.
c: Final Stuff leaders' debate, saying Labour would keep the super age at 65.

q: Winston Peters regularly says outrageous things, desperate for attention. He's not contributing constructively to political debate in New Zealand.
c: Speaking to reporters outside North Shore Hospital, after Peters said he should be jailed over the Covid response (RNZ live blog).

q: We're going to make sure the people that concoct them are no longer wasting people's time.
c: Reacting to the 1News–Verian poll, which he called 'crap', and saying NZ First would 'do something about the TV1 polls' after the election.

q: You've got members of Parliament saying the gangs are justified in their behaviour, because they're the victim of what? Colonisation? I've never heard such a disgraceful statement made.
c: Speaking to media in Auckland about political tension and safety (RNZ live blog).

q: Chris Hipkins was measurably the worst health Minister in modern New Zealand history, capable of vaporising billions of taxpayer dollars while healthcare performance got worse.
c: X post responding to Hipkins' challenge to debate health (opening text; posted 10:51am NZDT).

q: But your electorate vote, I would vote for the person who would answer my phone call at 5 o'clock on a Friday if I really had trouble and needed my local MP to help.
c: Nelson public meeting, endorsing National's Blair Cameron for the Nelson electorate (RNZ, published 21 Oct).

q: Stop railroading children into thinking that university is the only path to success.
c: Launching ACT's trades training policy at the Skills Institute in Wiri.

q: Another glossy document and another review won't fix a single ED. Labour had six years to get this right, and performance went backwards on its watch.
c: Responding to Labour's emergency-department plan.

q: I want to be clear: we are not here to prop up the current coalition government. If that coalition agreement was put in front of us, we would have walked away.
c: Morning Report interview (RNZ live blog).

q: We will reach out if he doesn't call us and give him one last chance to have that conversation, and if he doesn't want to, if he really wants to be in opposition, then we will go and speak to Labour next.
c: On Luxon ruling Opportunity out, after the 1News–Verian poll.

q: As I said, I've ruled out Opportunity. I don't know how to be any clearer about it.
c: To 1News in Pongakawa, after a supporter said they expected him to work with Opportunity after the election.

q: Maths is an important life skill which opens doors to jobs, qualifications and a more prosperous future so we want every child to gain those skills.
c: Announcing National's plan to expand the Maths Acceleration Programme.

q: Yes, they are, but you're making record returns under a National government so just be thankful for something, why don't we be thankful for something.
c: Replying to a resident at a cow shed near Edgecumbe who said dairy-farm costs were going up.

q: I know you guys don't like to admit that your competitors might have a point, but if you look at the Freshwater poll that was carried by The Post yesterday, it said exactly the opposite.
c: Asked in Hamilton about Labour's fall in the 1News–Verian poll.

q: We can't go back on that decision, but we can figure out a way forward that protects New Zealand's aluminium industry, and we'll look to do that with a degree of urgency.
c: Visiting an aluminium plant in Hamilton, on the government's rejection of import safeguards (RNZ live blog).

q: I have been in government with that collection of people ... And once you've had that bitter experience, you're never going to go back again.
c: NZ Herald Powerbrokers' debate, asked whether he could work with Labour under Kieran McAnulty or Barbara Edmonds. (RNZ's live blog transcribed 'bitter' as 'better'.)

q: No, no ... as a child, I got a few smackings and guess what? I thoroughly deserved them. Make no bones about it.
c: NZ Herald Powerbrokers' debate, asked about NZ First's position on the anti-smacking law.

q: We believe that the child should have a chance to grow up and make a decision. Not have a decision made for it and regret it for the rest of his life.
c: After the High Court set aside the government's puberty-blocker restrictions, saying the ruling should be appealed (RNZ live blog).

q: I believe it will come back in five years, ten years, sooner or later that tension needs to be resolved, but I'm not campaigning on it this election.
c: NZ Herald Powerbrokers' debate, on his Treaty Principles Bill (RNZ live blog).

q: There's no limit to what you can achieve if you don't care who takes the credit.
c: After the Powerbrokers' debate, asked what advice he had for Luxon and Hipkins on reaching cross-party agreement.

q: It's really ordinary for people to feel wigged out many times as a parent of young children, but I think that where we have to be putting our emphasis is in all of us supporting each other to just end violence of all forms towards any child.
c: After the Powerbrokers' debate, responding to Peters' comments about being smacked as a child.

q: Any politician in any political party in any government that is putting up unnecessary barriers to people engaging in the political process is actively engaging in voter suppression, especially when there is not a leg to stand on when it comes to rationale as to why.
c: Speaking to reporters in central Auckland about the end of same-day enrolment (RNZ live blog).

q: The point of this exercise was just to demonstrate that something can sound really good on the political hustings when it comes to taking tax off this or that but it is really important we have thorough economic analysis so people understand the distributional impacts.
c: On Green-commissioned analysis of ACT's KiwiSaver tax policy.

q: I think it's completely disrespectful and inappropriate for our political leaders to be talking that way in a country like New Zealand, where we are so proud of our multi culture.
c: NZ Herald Powerbrokers' debate, responding to Peters' 'diversity is weakness' remarks (RNZ live blog).

q: Kiwis and parents can see the transformation of our education system with these reforms. They can see it in their children, they know that it's working.
c: On the 1News–Verian finding that 70% back the hour-a-day reading, writing and maths rule.

q: By no means is the health system fixed, but we are heading in the right direction.
c: Morning Report health debate with Labour's Ayesha Verrall.

q: Not every senior can - or wants to - move to a retirement village. New Zealand needs many more low cost, affordable pensioner housing units.
c: Announcing National's housing pledge for older people at Pacific Lakes Retirement Village, Papamoa.

q: We know many families want to embrace inter-generational living, but councils make it too difficult.
c: On extending granny-flat rules to tiny homes and empty sections.

q: I have not asked her for a detailed breakdown of every interaction that she's had with members of her own family, but she did say yesterday that she had not visited a gang pad as part of her election campaigning, and I have absolutely accepted that.
c: In Napier, asked about candidate Kerrin Leoni's contact with Mongrel Mob members.

q: If you really want to be tough on gangs, fix drug addiction because that's where they're making all of their money.
c: Answering a question on Māori imprisonment at the Hawke's Bay Chamber of Commerce (RNZ live blog).

q: So I made a very clear line of saying: if something's underway, funded, let's keep it moving because there's no point of constantly changing our priorities all the time.
c: Hawke's Bay Chamber of Commerce, on not stopping infrastructure projects already underway (RNZ live blog).

q: Our justice system and sentencing regime needs to work properly, while ensuring that victims of crime are prioritised over offenders.
c: Announcing NZ First's law-and-order package in West Auckland.

q: Those countries are equal with us. We don't talk down. We don't look down to them. We treat them as equal.
c: On criticism of the Pacific Islands Forum's decision to make Israel a partner (RNZ live blog).

q: There is no one type of charter school for one type of student, and that is the point.
c: Announcing ACT's target of 10,000 charter school enrolments by 2029, in Henderson.

q: Here's a little political reality: 10,000 students at charter schools means 20,000 parents, means 40,000 grandparents, means 60,000 voters or 2 percent of all voters.
c: Speaking to media at North West College, Henderson (RNZ live blog).

q: New Zealanders know that inflation was getting back under control under this government until someone invaded a country with a strait called Hormuz ...
c: Responding to the September-quarter inflation figures (RNZ live blog).

q: Epsom has always had a strategy, but Epsom has never been only a strategy. You do actually have to want the job, and do the job, and be up there representing people day by day, whether you think it's to your electoral advantage or not.
c: Epsom candidates' debate, replying to Paul Goldsmith's two-ticks pitch.

q: Someone is profiting handsomely from driving people into more and more conflict.
c: Morning Report, on threats and abuse directed at MPs and the role of social media algorithms (RNZ live blog).

q: We have been fixing the underlying foundations, and New Zealand will be seeing the rewards if we stick to the plan.
c: Media stand-up on the September-quarter inflation figures (RNZ live blog).

q: I have actually felt relatively safe, I've been really supported by the police.
c: In Christchurch, asked about candidate safety after the attack on Australian MP Helen Haines (RNZ live blog).

q: All of us navigate family situations in politics, and it's bloody hard.
c: Hawke's Bay A&P show, on Kerrin Leoni's resignation as a Labour candidate.

q: It is a clear violation of the very clear standards that I have set out for our MPs and candidates. Her position had become untenable.
c: Hawke's Bay A&P show, on Leoni's resignation.

q: Our Māori MPs get held to a very different standard to others.
c: Media stand-up on the reaction to Leoni's resignation.

q: It's a crime issue, law and order issue, not a race issue.
c: Rejecting Hipkins' claim that racism was a factor in the Leoni affair (RNZ live blog).

q: I mean, the video didn't look like a family gathering. It looked like someone in Labour Party gear campaigning.
c: Hawke's Bay A&P show, asked whether Leoni was the victim of a pile-on (RNZ live blog).

q: Children in poverty cannot eat a surplus.
c: Releasing the Green Party's fiscal plan at Parliament.

q: Come on Nicola, let's get our credentials and credibility and put them to the test. If you've got anything to say about our plan, which I'm sure you will, come and say it to my face.
c: Challenging Nicola Willis to a fiscal debate.

q: It is a choice between financial security or financial ruin.
c: Responding to the Greens' fiscal plan.

q: I think she has revealed that what's good for the goose is good for the gangster.
c: Daily media conference, on Kerrin Leoni's resignation (RNZ live blog).

q: We don't want to be salivating over somebody else's misery.
c: Speaking to reporters after NZ First's depreciation announcement, on Leoni's resignation (RNZ live blog).

q: We've got to export, export, export, as we always have to.
c: Announcing NZ First's 50% accelerated depreciation policy at Pact Packaging, East Tāmaki.

q: Our whānau do not stop being our whānau because they wear a patch, and our responsibility to them does not disappear because someone finds their presence politically inconvenient.
c: Te Pāti Māori statement after Kerrin Leoni's resignation.

q: She did not want to get in the way of us trying to get rid of this rotten government, and she knew the Nats would come after her if she stayed a candidate.
c: Facebook post on Leoni's resignation, as Labour's Māori campaign chair (reported by RNZ).

q: There is a responsibility for all of us in politics to understand the power and the influence of our platform.
c: Interview with Mata with Mihingarangi Forbes, on the attack on Australian MP Helen Haines (published by RNZ).

q: A party vote for National is the only way to stop Chlöe Swarbrick becoming our Minister of Finance and introducing a wealth tax, an inheritance tax, higher corporate taxes...
c: Press conference as National's campaign chair, attacking the Greens' fiscal plan (RNZ live blog).

q: He's not campaigning, he's not fundraising, he's not raising funds for the Mongrel Mob.
c: Auckland media conference, defending National MP Tama Potaka over a photo with gang members.

q: I think it'd be disingenuous to suggest that they are equivalent images that we've seen.
c: Comparing the Potaka photo with images of Labour, Green and Te Pāti Māori candidates with Mongrel Mob members.

q: Good habits start early, and kids should be able to save their birthday money, put away their pocket money, and of course start building good money habits as soon as possible.
c: Launching National's 'plan for parents' in Auckland (NZ Herald report via Newstalk ZB).

q: I think there's a lot of packaging up of things that we have announced already.
c: Asked whether the 'plan for parents' contained anything new (NZ Herald report via Newstalk ZB).

q: He now needs to answer why he thinks National MPs should be held to a different standard to the standard he demands of others.
c: Queensgate Mall, Lower Hutt, on Luxon's defence of Tama Potaka.

q: Couldn't say. Quite possibly. I mean, how would you know, some of the time?
c: Asked whether he had ever been photographed with a gang member.

q: I'm astounded to have those claims from Christopher Luxon today, if anyone is exhibiting they have a massive double standard, it's Christopher Luxon.
c: Responding to Luxon's claim that Labour was inconsistent on gang association (NZ Herald report via Newstalk ZB).

q: The cost of living is the number one issue in this year's election campaign.
c: Lower Hutt stand-up promoting Labour's cost of living action plan (RNZ live blog).

q: Instead of just learning about investment in a textbook, students will have real skin in the game.
c: Announcing ACT's $500 investment account for every Year 11 student.

q: Young New Zealanders will see themselves not just as workers and consumers, but as investors and owners with a stake in our country's success.
c: ACT's financial education policy announcement.

q: There is no substitute for diesel for industry. Likewise, ordinary consumers have suffered too much with the cost of petrol.
c: Public meeting in Thames, announcing NZ First's plan to remove the ETS charge from fuel (RNZ live blog).

q: We are in the Green Party very, very committed to our values and our principles, which look like appropriate decision making, which look like restorative justice, which look like a commitment to evidence-based policy.
c: Armageddon Expo, Auckland, asked whether she was comfortable with the standard Hipkins has set on gangs (NZ Herald report via Newstalk ZB).

q: The right benefits every time we turn on each other, and we will not give them that victory.
c: Statement after Kerrin Leoni's resignation, distancing Te Pāti Māori from its role in her downfall (NZ Herald report via Newstalk ZB, 24 Oct).
